source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®;
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning in all the arrangements of God was present to men, and announced future things and showed present things and told past things, judges indeed all, but is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the creature more than the Creator, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, nor willing to go free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law at an unseasonable time, needing nothing from God, and not recognizing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, nor willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of him: one indeed, made in a human being in a plague, knowing to bear weakness, and sitting on a foal of an ass, and a stone rejected by the builders, and led like a sheep to sacrifice, and dissolving Amalech by the extension of hands; gathering however the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and remembering his own dead who slept, and descending to them, so that he might rescue them;

pass_b_english: The spiritual disciple who truly receives the Spirit of God—who from the beginning was present to humanity in all God's arrangements, who announced things to come, revealed present realities, and explained the past—judges all people yet is judged by no one. He judges the nations, creatures who serve the creation rather than the Creator and who, with a reprobate mind, waste their entire effort in futility. He also judges the Jews, who fail to perceive the word of liberty and refuse to go free even though a liberator stands before them; they pretend to serve God outside the Law at the wrong time, as if God needed anything, and they refuse to recognize Christ's advent, accomplished for human salvation, or to understand that all the prophets announced his two comings. The first came when he was made man in affliction, knowing how to bear weakness, riding on a donkey's colt (Zechariah 9:9), rejected as a stone by the builders (Psalms 118:22), led like a sheep to slaughter (Isaiah 53:7), and overthrowing Amalek by the stretching out of his hands; yet also gathering the scattered children from the ends of the earth into the Father's fold, remembering his own dead who had fallen asleep, and descending to them so that he might rescue them.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required scripture citations for the prophetic allusions (Zechariah 9:9, Psalms 118:22, Isaiah 53:7) which were present in the sense of the Latin but not explicitly cited in the source text, fulfilling the requirement to identify them. Pass A and B are consistent with the Latin source.
